speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to help narrow this down, are you currently experiencing a sore throat or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis). The combination of a pruritic rash, fever, and the specific description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area is highly suggestive of scarlet fever, likely triggered by the recent viral prodrome. REQUEST TEST: Throat_Culture and Rapid_Strep_Antigen.
